claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I'm inquiring about my child. I have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, let me ask you: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially towards their upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like clothes and other expenses they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help me assess your eligibility properly, I need to know a bit more detail about your financial contributions:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each month (or week), and is this amount at least equal to the Child Benefit payment?**

(For reference, Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, which is about £110.93 per month)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information. Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex** (for example, the person Alex lives with)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**How long has Alex been living away from you?** (This will help me determine if you're still within the eligibility period or if your ongoing contributions continue to qualify you)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been living away from me for quite a while now - it's been a few years actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 8 years old, which is under the age limit of 16
- You live in the UK
- Although Alex doesn't live with you, you are considered responsible for Alex because you contribute £30 per week towards their upkeep
- Your contribution exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child), which means you meet the financial responsibility requirement
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Since you're contributing at least as much as the Child Benefit rate towards Alex's upkeep (through clothes and other expenses), you qualify as being responsible for the child under the Child Benefit rules.

**Next steps:** You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. You'll need to apply through the official government channels.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.
